question_html: "Fixed Asset held for sale" will be classified in the Balance Sheet as per Schedule III of the Companies Act as:
answer_html: Answer: (B) Current Asset — an asset held for sale (expected to be realised/converted to cash within the normal operating cycle or 12 months) is classified as a current asset under Schedule III, regardless of its original non-current classification while in use.

question_html: Past Ltd. had the following items under the head "Reserves and Surplus" the Balance Sheet as on 31st March 2025 (Amount ₹ in lakhs): Securities Premium Account 90; Capital Reserve 40; Revaluation Reserve 70. The company had an accumulated loss of ₹280 lakhs on the same date, which was disclosed under the head "Statement of Profit and Loss" as asset in Balance Sheet. What should be disclosed on the face of Balance Sheet as per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Reserve and Surplus-Securities premium 90 lakhs; others ₹ 110 lakh and Accumulated loss ₹ 280 lakhs in the Asset side.
options.B: Reserve and Surplus ₹ 200 lakhs; and Accumulated loss ₹ 280 lakhs in the Asset side.

topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.5): Negative Reserves and Surplus presentation - netting accumulated loss against reserves

question_html: A Ltd. has a balance of ₹17,15,000 in the loan account with State Finance Corporation which is inclusive of ₹1,15,000 for interest accrued but not due. The loan is secured by hypothecation of the Plant and Machinery. As per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 loan is to be disclosed in the balance sheet as follows:

options.A: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings.
options.B: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and ₹1,15,000 under short-term borrowings.
options.C: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and ₹1,15,000 under other current liabilities.
options.D: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and no disclosure for ₹1,15,000.

answer_html: Answer: (C) — the principal loan balance, net of the interest component (₹17,15,000 − ₹1,15,000 = ₹16,00,000), stays under Long-Term Borrowings (secured, hypothecation-backed). Interest accrued but not yet due is not itself a "borrowing" — per Schedule III it is disclosed separately under Other Current Liabilities, not lumped into long-term borrowings and not mislabelled as a short-term borrowing (which would imply it is itself a loan).
topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.5): Interest accrued but not due on a secured loan disclosed under Other Current Liabilities, separate from the long-term borrowings principal

question_html: Glow Limited had taken a loan of ₹5,00,000 in June, 2023. The loan is to be repaid in 10 half yearly equal installments starting from December, 2023. Determine how the remaining loan will be classified in the Balance Sheet as on 31st March, 2024 as per Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: ₹3,50,000 is to be shown under the head 'Long term borrowings and ₹1,00,000 is to be shown under the head 'Short term borrowings"
options.B: ₹3,50,000 is to be shown under the head 'Long term borrowings and ₹75,000 is to be shown under the head "Short term borrowings" and ₹25,000 is to be shown under the head 'Other Current liabilities."
options.C: ₹4,50,000 is to be shown under the head 'Long term borrowings'
options.D: ₹3,50,000 is to be shown under the head 'Long term borrowings' and ₹1,00,000 is to be shown under the head 'Other Current liabilities.'

answer_html:
Answer: the source's printed Answer Key states (A). Working: instalments of ₹50,000 each fall due Dec 2023, Jun 2024, Dec 2024 ... Jun 2028 (10 total). One instalment (Dec 2023) is paid before the 31 March 2024 balance sheet date, leaving ₹4,50,000 outstanding, of which the Jun 2024 and Dec 2024 instalments (₹1,00,000) fall due within the next 12 months and ₹3,50,000 remains due beyond 12 months.

Flagging an independent-derivation discrepancy: per Note 6(A) to Schedule III's General Instructions for the Balance Sheet, "current maturities of long-term debt" are disclosed as a separate line item under 'Other Current Liabilities', not under 'Short-term borrowings' — which would point to option (D), not (A), for the ₹1,00,000 due within 12 months. This exact classification point ("current-vs-long-term loan classification") is even called out as a worked example in this repo's own AS-index for the Schedule III unit. We are not overriding the source's printed answer letter (A) — it is reproduced verbatim — but flagging this as a possible inconsistency in the source's own key for Pranav's judgment, per the never-silently-fix rule.
topic_text: Schedule III (1.5): Schedule III balance sheet presentation, incl. current-vs-long-term loan classification

question_html: Past Ltd. had the following items under the head "Reserves and Surplus" the Balance Sheet as on 31st March 2025: (Amount ₹ in lakhs) Securities Premium Account 90; Capital Reserve 40; Revaluation Reserve 70. The company had an accumulated loss of ₹280 lakhs on the same date, which was disclosed under the head "Statement of Profit and Loss" as asset in Balance Sheet. What should be disclosed on the face of Balance Sheet as per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Reserve and Surplus-Securities premium 90 lakhs; others ₹110 lakh and Accumulated loss ₹280 lakhs in the Asset side.
options.B: Reserve and Surplus ₹200 lakhs; and Accumulated loss ₹280 lakhs in the Asset side.

answer_html: Answer: (D) Reserve and Surplus − ₹80 lakhs only. Schedule III does not permit an accumulated loss (a debit balance in the Statement of Profit and Loss) to be shown as an asset. It must instead be netted directly within the "Reserves and Surplus" line on the equity side: total credit-balance reserves (₹90 + ₹40 + ₹70 = ₹200 lakhs) less the accumulated loss (₹280 lakhs) = a net negative ₹80 lakhs, disclosed as "Reserves and Surplus − ₹80 lakhs" (a negative figure within Reserves and Surplus, not a positive asset-side item).
topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.5): An accumulated loss exceeding available reserves is netted within Reserves and Surplus as a negative balance, never shown as an asset

question_html: "Fixed Asset held for sale" will be classified in the Balance Sheet as per Schedule III of the Companies Act as:
answer_html: Answer: (B) Current Asset — a fixed asset retired from active use and held for disposal is no longer part of the entity's productive non-current asset base; it is expected to be realised/converted to cash within the normal operating cycle, and is accordingly reclassified and shown as a current asset (at the lower of net book value and net realisable value) under Schedule III.
topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.5): Schedule III classification of assets retired from active use and held for disposal

question_html: As per Rule 7 of the Companies (Declaration & Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014, in the event of inadequacy or absence of profits in any year, a Company may declare dividend out of surplus subject to the condition that the total amount drawn from accumulated profits shall not exceed ___________ as appearing in the latest audited financial statement.

options.B: 1/5th of the sum of its paid-up share capital
options.C: 1/10th of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves
options.D: 1/5th of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves

answer_html: Answer: (C) 1/10th of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves.
topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.6): Dividend Rules cap on withdrawal from accumulated reserves

question_html: A Ltd. has a balance of ₹17,15,000 in the loan account with State Finance Corporation which is inclusive of ₹1,15,000 for interest accrued but not due. The loan is secured by hypothecation of the Plant and Machinery. As per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 loan is to be disclosed in the balance sheet as follows:

options.A: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings.
options.B: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and ₹1,15,000 under short-term borrowings.
options.C: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and ₹1,15,000 under other current liabilities.
options.D: Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and no disclosure for ₹1,15,000.

answer_html: Answer: (c) Disclosed ₹16,00,000 as a secured loan under long-term borrowings and ₹1,15,000 under other current liabilities. The principal loan balance (₹17,15,000 − ₹1,15,000 interest accrued but not due = ₹16,00,000) is a long-term secured borrowing. Per Schedule III's format, "interest accrued but not due on borrowings" is not itself a borrowing (long-term or short-term) – it is separately classified under "Other current liabilities."
topic_text: Preparation of Financial Statements (1.5): Interest accrued but not due on borrowings is classified under Other Current Liabilities, separate from the borrowing itself
